additions.name: CtrlS Hyderabad Financial District datacenter — existing operations (operator-mapped facility, DC2 or DC3)

status.summary: CtrlS's company blog post of 24 September 2026 states that 'Its three Hyderabad datacenters support requirements ranging from individual racks and secure cages to dedicated halls'. CtrlS's releases of 29 May 2024 and 20 January 2025 say its three Hyderabad facilities are one in HITEC City and two in the Financial District, Gachibowli (including DC3), and the Hyderabad page lists DC 1 to DC 3, so the operator-mapped Financial District facility is among the three that were in service on 24 September 2026. This records continuing operation on that date, not an opening date (DC3 was launched on 29 May 2024 and DC2 in 2020). No capacity in service, occupancy or later phase is established.

locator.precision: This is the operator-linked named Google Maps place 'CtrlS data center' (feature 0x3bcb93279e17eb1b:0x3f1aebcc1ae9ec8f) that CtrlS's Hyderabad page links as its map location, used as the locator of CtrlS's Financial District datacenter property. It marks one of CtrlS's two Financial District facilities (DC2 or DC3) and does not give a building footprint, plot boundary or entrance, resolve which of the two it marks, or locate DC1 in HITEC City.
locator.identity_review: CtrlS's Hyderabad Data Centers page (version of 22 September 2026, unchanged in the Internet Archive copy of 1 October 2026 and present in the 29 August 2026 copy of the previous version) lists Hyderabad DC 1, DC 2 and DC 3 and links its 'Map Location' control to https://maps.app.goo.gl/UJkTsDZruw3MyvbMA, which resolves to the named place 'CtrlS data center' with place coordinates 17.4233287, 78.3303868 (!3d/!4d, echoed in the place payload). CtrlS's releases of 29 May 2024 and 20 January 2025 put one Hyderabad facility in HITEC City and two, including DC3, in the Financial District, Gachibowli; the about-us timeline dates the first Hyderabad facility, PTDC, to 2008 and DC2 to 2020; PTDC appears from its name and the Pioneer Towers registered office in Madhapur to be the HITEC City facility, which would make the two Financial District facilities DC2 and DC3 (an inference; the operator does not map DC1 or DC2 separately). The mapped place lies in the Gachibowli/Nanakramguda Financial District area of west Hyderabad, about 5.9 km west-south-west of the ITPH campus in HITEC City and away from the registered office in Madhapur, so it marks DC2 or DC3; the link follows the page's DC3 tour and DC3 resilience sections, but the page does not say which facility it marks. Esri World Imagery (captured 22 October 2026) shows the point on a large multi-storey building with dense rooftop plant beside a second plant-heavy building about 100 m to the south-east. The viewport centre @17.4228236,78.3274561 (316 m west) and the head-office address are not used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The operator-linked map place publishes no surveyed horizontal accuracy, and no official address point or plot boundary for CtrlS's Financial District facilities was found; the place may stand for either of two facilities whose separation is not published.

additions.distinctness_review: Screened all serialized fields of the sites, projects, evidence, source records and identity mapping of verified_construction_core/2026-10-23-research-fortyfourth (594 sites, 629 projects, 3,213 evidence rows; re-screened by the verifier after the base advanced from the forty-third release), every sources/*-holds.json file and the pending queue fragments for CtrlS, Ctrl S, PTDC, Hyderabad DC, DC2, DC3, Gachibowli, Nanakramguda and Financial District. CtrlS matches only the imported CtrlS Chandanvelly AI-ready data center park (announced campus at the Chandanvelly locality, 27.0 km south-west), the CtrlS Kolkata New Town campus and their evidence, and holds for CtrlS Patna, Bodh Gaya and the APIIC Rambilli allotment; none is a Hyderabad Financial District facility. The other terms match no record (DC3 hits are other operators' building names and hash strings). No Atlas site, project, source-record or identity-mapping coordinate lies within 2 km of the point: the nearest are CapitaLand DC ITPH Hyderabad (5.85 km, a different operator's campus in HITEC City), AdaniConneX Hyderabad (14.4 km, locality point), TCS HyperVault (16.8 km, locality point) and AirTrunk HYD1 and CtrlS Chandanvelly (27.0 km, shared locality point). No pending fragment proposes a CtrlS or Hyderabad Financial District record. Sify's Hyderabad datacenter (Survey No. 115/1, Financial District, Nanakramguda) is a different operator's facility that is not in the Atlas and is held here for want of a locator.
additions.successor_review: 24 September 2026 is 29 days before 23 October 2026 and stays inside the 90-day window until 23 December 2026. CtrlS's post sitemap captured on 22 October 2026 lists after 24 September only market-commentary blogs (28 and 29 September, 1, 7 and 19 October), the 16 October Kolkata-Visakhapatnam article and the 16 October Patna release, none of which reports a pause, closure or change at the Hyderabad facilities; the Hyderabad page re-captured on 22 October still lists DC 1 to DC 3 and the same map link. No later status statement was found.

scoped_project_details.facility_scope: The CtrlS datacenter at the operator-mapped Financial District location in Hyderabad, one of CtrlS's two Financial District facilities (DC2, launched 2020; DC3, launched 29 May 2024). DC1 (PTDC, HITEC City) and the planned Chandanvalley and Future City campuses are separate and not part of this project.
scoped_project_details.capacity_note: The Hyderabad page gives power capacity of 7.4 MW for DC 2 and 13 MW for DC 3 (13 MW IT load per the May 2024 release); because the marked facility is not resolved, no capacity is recorded.
scoped_project_details.operating_statement_date: 2026-09-24 (operator blog); page version 2026-09-22 corroborates the three-facility listing

additions.name: CtrlS Bengaluru Datacenter — existing operations

status.summary: CtrlS's Bengaluru Data Center page, in its version of 12 August 2026, invites customers to 'experience the unparalleled advantage of collocating at South India's leading datacenter that has a legacy of servicing some of the world's largest hyperscalers' and describes the Electronic City facility as a Rated-4, LEED Platinum v4 O+M (operations and maintenance) certified, B+G+7 storey datacenter of 2,000 racks and 13 MW IT power capacity with a 'Zero Downtime Record'. This records the facility as operating on 12 August 2026, the modification day of the captured version, not an inspection or opening date (the operator dates the Bengaluru launch to 2018). Capacity in service and occupancy are not established.

locator.precision: This is the operator-linked named Google Maps place 'Ctrls Datacenters Bangalore DC' (feature 0x3bae6c8c23b299c5:0xec3d8f241288b411) that CtrlS's Bengaluru page links as its map location, used as the locator of the single-building Electronic City datacenter property. It does not give the building footprint, plot boundary or entrance.
locator.identity_review: CtrlS's Bengaluru Data Center page (version of 12 August 2026; the Internet Archive copy of 3 August 2026 shows the previous version with the same facility text and link) describes one Bengaluru datacenter at 'Electronic city, Bengaluru' and links its 'Map Location' control to https://maps.app.goo.gl/BHKXeedvjm2T2va66, which resolves to the named place 'Ctrls Datacenters Bangalore DC' with place coordinates 12.8425375, 77.6712825 (!3d/!4d, echoed in the place payload; the viewport equals the place tuple). The operator's about-us timeline records '2018 Launched data center in Bangalore' and CtrlS names no other Bengaluru facility. Esri World Imagery (captured 22 October 2026) shows the point on a tall multi-storey building with rooftop plant, consistent with the B+G+7 storey building described. The page's proximity figures are not geocoded.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The operator-linked map place publishes no surveyed horizontal accuracy, and no official address point or plot boundary for the facility was found.

additions.successor_review: 12 August 2026 is 72 days before 23 October 2026 and stays inside the 90-day window until 10 November 2026. The live page captured on 22 October 2026 is the same 12 August version; none of the CtrlS posts listed in its post sitemap after 12 August (captured the same day and read) concerns the Bengaluru facility; they mention Bengaluru only as a market, and no pause, closure or redevelopment of the Bengaluru facility was found.

scoped_project_details.facility_scope: CtrlS's single Bengaluru datacenter building in Electronic City (Rated-4, B+G+7 storeys, 106,536 sq. ft. built-up, 2,000 racks)
scoped_project_details.capacity_note: The page states 'IT Power capacity - 13 MW'; this is the facility's stated design figure, not measured load, and is not recorded as a typed observation.
scoped_project_details.launch_year_per_operator: 2018 (about-us timeline; not used as a status observation)

status.summary: Sify's Chennai data-centre page, in its version of 29 September 2026, presents Chennai 02 in Siruseri as Sify's hyperscale campus 'with 25.92 MW IT Power' that 'onboards multiple telecom service providers, Internet Exchanges for robust telecom services to customers and enables enterprises to run their critical applications seamlessly'. This is a newer operator observation that the campus is in service. It does not say how much of the planned campus is built or whether further buildings remain to be developed, so the existing partially operational code is kept rather than upgraded to full operation; 25.92 MW is a stated campus figure, not measured load.

status_updates.identity_review: Same campus as the existing record: the page names Sify's 'Hyperscale Data Center campus, Chennai 02 in Siruseri', the campus of the imported record 'Sify Chennai 02 data center campus, Siruseri' (operator Sify Infinit Spaces Limited), whose partially operational status comes from the 16 October 2025 DRHP. The refresh keeps that campus-level scope and does not change the record's locality locator. Sify's separate Chennai 01 facility at Tidel Park, Taramani, described on the same page, is not touched.
status_updates.successor_review: Strictly newer than the existing 16 October 2025 observation. Sify's dedicated Chennai 02 page (modified 21 August 2026) gives the same 25.92 MW campus description. Sify's post sitemap captured on 22 October 2026 lists as its newest news item the 22 October appointment of a chief executive for Sify Infinit Spaces; no news item reports a pause, closure or completion of the full Chennai 02 campus, so the status is neither downgraded nor upgraded.
